cueCard.topic: Describe an old object that your family has kept for a long time.
cueCard.explain: and explain why your family has kept it.

questions.text: Describe an old object that your family has kept for a long time.
questions.say: Thank you. Now, in Part 2, I'm going to give you a topic, and I'd like you to talk about it for one to two minutes. Before you talk, you'll have one minute to think about what you're going to say. You can make some notes if you wish. Here is your topic. Describe an old object that your family has kept for a long time. You should say: what it is; where it came from; where it is kept now; and explain why your family has kept it.

questions.text: Would you like to keep this object yourself one day?
questions.say: Thank you. Would you like to keep this object yourself one day?

questions.text: Why are some people interested in their family history?
questions.say: Thank you. We've been talking about an old object that your family has kept for a long time, and I'd like to discuss with you some more general questions related to this. Let's consider first of all family history. Why are some people interested in their family history?

questions.text: How do families in your country pass their history on to children?

questions.text: Is it important for young people to know about their grandparents' lives?

questions.text: Why do some people keep things they no longer use?
questions.say: Now let's talk about keeping things. Why do some people keep things they no longer use?

questions.text: Do people today keep fewer things than in the past?
